title: Maintenance of serotonin in the intestinal mucosa and ganglia of mice that lack the high-affinity serotonin transporter: Abnormal intestinal motility and the expression of cation transporters
authors: Chen JJ, Li Z, Pan H, Murphy DL, Tamir H, Koepsell H, et al.
population: Mice with targeted deletion of the serotonin transporter (SERT) and wild-type littermates
funder: This work was supported by Grant NS12969 from the National Institute of Neurological Diseases and Stroke.
result: In wild-type bowel, SERT mediated high-affinity serotonin uptake into epithelial cells, mast cells and enteric neurons; this uptake was absent without SERT, leaving only lower-affinity transport by the dopamine transporter and organic cation transporters OCT-1 and OCT-3. Serotonin remained in all normal gut sites but was absent from blood. Stool water and colonic motility were increased in most SERT-deficient mice (diarrhoea), occasionally alternating with decreased motility (constipation). Animal data.
